_meta.description: Legal basis mapping for the 22 GDPR-derived privacy-policy criteria used by the GDPR Compliance Gap Evaluator.
_meta.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), as retained in UK law as the UK GDPR and supplemented by the Data Protection Act 2018.
_meta.caveat: A privacy policy is a transparency document, not the processing itself. Many criteria describe controller obligations that the policy should reflect, not obligations the policy itself discharges. This mapping identifies the provision that gives rise to the obligation, not a finding of legal compliance.
_meta.duplicate_note: 'Data Processing Records' and 'Records of Processing Activities' both derive from Article 30 GDPR. They are retained as separate criteria in the original list but should be collapsed or explicitly distinguished in implementation.

criteria.note: Article 30 requires controllers and processors to maintain records of processing activities, including purposes, categories of data and recipients. This is the same legal basis as 'Records of Processing Activities'; the two criteria are duplicative.

primary_legal_basis.title: Chapter III — Rights of the data subject

related_provisions: Articles 15–22 (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, automated decisions)
criteria.note: The policy should explain how data subjects can exercise their rights. Article 12 governs the manner; Articles 15–22 set out the substantive rights.

Article 7 requires the controller to demonstrate consent, to allow withdrawal and to ensure consent is freely given. The policy should describe the consent mechanism, not merely state that consent is used.
Personal data must be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in an incompatible manner. The policy should define those purposes.

related_provisions: Article 25 (data protection by design and by default)
criteria.note: Personal data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes. The policy should state that only necessary data are collected.
Article 32 requires appropriate technical and organisational measures, including encryption and access controls where appropriate. The policy should outline those measures at a meaningful level.

primary_legal_basis.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject

criteria.note: Article 33 requires notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours where feasible; Article 34 requires communication to data subjects where there is high risk. The policy should describe the response procedure.
A DPIA is required where processing is likely to result in a high risk to rights and freedoms, particularly using new technologies. The policy should explain when and how DPIAs are conducted.

primary_legal_basis.title: Transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations

criteria.note: Article 44 permits a transfer only if the Chapter V conditions are met. The policy should address international transfers and the safeguard relied on.

Duplicates 'Data Processing Records'. Both criteria map to Article 30. Implementers should either merge them or distinguish one as the policy commitment and the other as the operational record-keeping obligation.

primary_legal_basis.title: Designation of the data protection officer
Position of the data protection officer
Tasks of the data protection officer

criteria.note: A DPO is mandatory only in specified cases (public authority, large-scale systematic monitoring, large-scale special-category processing). The policy should state whether a DPO is appointed and provide contact details where applicable.

related_provisions: Article 29 (processing under the authority of controller or processor)
criteria.note: Article 28 requires a written contract or other legal act with processors, containing the mandatory terms in Article 28(3). The policy should disclose the use of processors and the safeguards applied.

primary_legal_basis.title: Tasks of the data protection officer — awareness-raising and training

related_provisions: Article 47(2)(j) (training under binding corporate rules, where relevant)
criteria.note: There is no single standalone 'training' article for all controllers. Article 39(1)(b) places training within the DPO's tasks; Article 32(4) treats staff training as part of appropriate organisational security measures. The policy should state that staff are trained.

primary_legal_basis.title: Time limits and modalities for responding to data subject requests

criteria.note: Article 12(3) requires a response without undue delay and in any event within one month. The policy should explain how requests are submitted and handled.

related_provisions: Article 17 (right to erasure / 'right to be forgotten')
Article 30(1)(f) (records should include envisaged time limits for erasure)
criteria.note: Article 5(1)(e) requires that data be kept no longer than necessary. The policy should define retention periods and secure deletion procedures.

primary_legal_basis.title: Data protection by design and by default

criteria.note: Article 25 requires technical and organisational measures designed to implement data protection principles and to process only necessary data by default. The policy should state that privacy is built into processing.

The GDPR does not prescribe a specific 'policy updates' procedure. The obligation is derived from transparency and accountability: changes that affect processing should be communicated to data subjects. The policy should describe how revisions are made and notified.

related_provisions: Article 33 (breach notification to the supervisory authority)
Article 30 (records made available to the supervisory authority on request)
criteria.note: Article 31 requires controllers and processors to cooperate with the supervisory authority on request. The policy should acknowledge reporting and cooperation obligations.

Article 33(5) requires the controller to document all personal data breaches, including the facts, effects and remedial action taken. This documentation enables the supervisory authority to verify compliance.

Article 5(2) makes the controller responsible for, and able to demonstrate, compliance. Article 24 gives that principle operational effect. The policy should outline governance measures demonstrating compliance.

related_provisions: Article 12(1) (concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form; clear and plain language)
criteria.note: Article 12(1) requires information to be provided in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. The policy should be easy for stakeholders to find and understand.

related_provisions: Article 6(1)(a)–(f) (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests)
criteria.note: Article 6 sets out the six lawful bases for processing. For special categories, Article 9 imposes additional conditions. The policy should explain the legal grounds relied on for each processing purpose.
